newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-VW seeks surge in 1998 Golf sales.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-VW seeks surge in 1998 Golf sales.

text.p: Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday that it expects to sell nearly a million of its popular Golf vehicles in 1998 and the vast majority will be the new fourth generation set to go on sale in October.
VW unveiled the new Golf at a reception on Tuesday and company officials said the car will help boost sales at the world's fourth largest carmaker into the next century.
"With the new Golf, we will maintain and build our leading position in Europe," said VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer. "The Golf will clearly remain at the top."

The Wolfsburg-based carmaker, which sold about 820,000 Golfs last year around the world, said it expected to sell about 700,000 of the new Golf models next year. The balance of sales will come from the current model, which is still being sold in North and South America, as well as in Asia.

VW has set ambitious growth plans for the new Golf, announcing plans for 1998 sales in Europe of about 700,000 in a bid to keep its leading market position against rivals General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co.

VW sources also said on Tuesday that VW plans to boost annual output to up to two million vehicles in the mid-term. VW will meet expected growth for the Golf, which accounts for about half of all Volkswagen vehicles, without having to build new factories, or boost its full-time workforce, they said.

The German carmaker said it would aggressively price the new Golf under the current model, announcing a base price for the new model at 25,700 marks -- about 400 marks cheaper than a comparable model despite a series of new standard equipment.
"I think that our customers will be pleasantly surprised when they see the value of the new Golf for the price," said VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech.

Volkswagen has put considerable effort into designing the new Golf, which made its debut in March 1974 to replace the popular Beetle model. It has been the backbone of VW's sales and nearly 18 million have now been produced.

While the new Golf shows a lot of family resemblance, the car has been revamped with bolder styling lines to make it longer and roomier than the current model, as well as to make important safety improvements, such as side air bags.
"It's what customers want," Piech has said about the new Golf compared with the current model. But he added, "It's a totally new car from top to bottom."

The new Golf will face a tough market in the compact class, in part due to the launch by Mercedes-Benz of the A-class subcompact and new model offerings from GM, such as the new Opel Astra due out next April, and the Ford Escort.
"I think VW will have to go beyond their normal market for the Golf and try to extend the reach with the new one," said Jonathan Storey at European Automotive Research in Britain.
"The new Golf is conservatively styled and that may be a problem. There are signs that the European market is ready for bolder designs. But the Golf will remain a leader."
